headline: Middle East, North Africa, Pakistan output to contract 1.3% in 2026 on US-Israel-Iran war
dek: IMF forecasts Middle East, North Africa and Pakistan output to contract 1.3% in 2026 due to the war's impact on energy production, shipping, tourism, trade and confidence; 6.6% rebound in 2027. Baseline assumes conflict abates early 2027; economies stay below pre-war projections.
sources: International Monetary Fund regional outlook (via Reuters)
fault_line: End the war to save the economy, or strike until Iran yields — who pays the 1.3%?

sections.what_happened: IMF forecasts Middle East, North Africa and Pakistan output to contract 1.3% in 2026 due to the war's impact on energy production, shipping, tourism, trade and confidence; 6.6% rebound in 2027. Baseline assumes conflict abates early 2027; economies stay below pre-war projections. Oil exporters hit harder by energy/shipping disruption; oil importers more resilient (remittances, tourism, policy responses). Main risk: further disruption to energy production and trade routes driving energy prices higher. 'Exceptionally high uncertainty.'
sections.what_disputed: The 2027 rebound rests on the baseline assumption that the conflict abates early 2027 — explicitly flagged as highly uncertain; further energy disruption worsens the outlook.
sections.why_matters: The IMF prices the war at -1.3% of an entire region's output — the pocketbook argument against Washington's post-election strike plans: oil exporters and shippers pay while the war planners face an election.
sections.context: Background: NEW — IMF regional outlook ( ): Middle East, North Africa, Pakistan output to contract 1.3% in 2026 on US-Israel-Iran war; 6.6% rebound in 2027

The fault line our audience is arguing over: End the war to save the economy, or strike until Iran yields — who pays the 1.3%?
